findings.issue_text: `totalPages` adds an extra page when `user_count` is exactly divisible by `limit`, causing an empty final member-list page.
Group creation ignores the submitted `alias_level`, so new groups retain the model default instead of the admin-selected setting.
`group.users.delete(user_id)` passes an integer where ActiveRecord expects a `User` record, causing an association type mismatch during member removal.
`/groups/:group_id/members.json` changes its response from a serialized array to an object, breaking API clients that expect the existing array response.

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group creation ignores the submitted `alias_level`, so new groups retain the model default instead of the admin-selected setting.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the create method in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb, the new code sets group.name and group.visible from params, but does NOT set group.alias_level. In contrast, the update method does handle alias_level: 'group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?'. The frontend template shows aliasLevelOptions being rendered with a combo-box for alias_level selection, and the asJSON function in the model includes alias_level. However, the create action in the controller ignores this parameter entirely, meaning new groups will always have the default alias_level (0) regardless of what the admin selects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `group.users.delete(user_id)` passes an integer where ActiveRecord expects a `User` record, causing an association type mismatch during member removal.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in the `remove_member` method of `Admin::GroupsController`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i`. The `delete` method on an ActiveRecord association like `group.users` (which is a has_many through or has_and_belongs_to_many) can accept either record objects or IDs. When you pass an integer ID to `delete`, ActiveRecord will find and remove the association record with that ID. This is documented behavior - `collection.delete(object, ...)` can accept objects or IDs. So this is not actually a bug - passing an integer user_id to `group.users.delete()` is valid and will work correctly to remove the user from the group.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `/groups/:group_id/members.json` changes its response from a serialized array to an object, breaking API clients that expect the existing array response.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb, the `members` action previously used `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` which would return a serialized array. After the change, it returns `render json: { members: serialize_data(members, GroupUserSerializer), meta: { total: total, limit: limit, offset: offset } }` which is an object with 'members' and 'meta' keys. This is indeed a breaking API change - any existing API clients expecting an array response would now receive an object instead. The finding correctly identifies this as a real compatibility issue.
